appraisal_events.evidence: il a gardé celui de baron de Charlus, par protestation et avec une apparente simplicité où il y a beaucoup d'orgueil... Il n'y a pas selon lui de titre plus ancien que celui de baron de Charlus... antérieur à celui des Montmorency
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup portrays his uncle as proudly distinguished by holding the family's oldest, most exclusive title rather than an inflated princely one, but his own framing of hidden pride and his dismissal of genealogy as tedious tempers the elevation with mild irony.

appraisal_events.evidence: il est grand ami de Swann et l'a toujours beaucoup soutenu
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup reports that Charlus is a great friend of Swann and has always strongly supported him, a fact reflecting positively on Swann through this powerful association.

status_effects.explanation: His deliberate choice of the family's most ancient title over grander available ones marks him as exceptionally, self-consciously distinguished, though the passage's irony about his pride tempers a fuller elevation.
Swann benefits from being described as long and strongly supported by the well-connected, aristocratically distinguished Charlus.
